exposure: Unexplained vaginal bleeding during second or third trimester
outcome: Diagnosis of bleeding source by colposcopy
Specific colposcopic findings (e.g., ectropion, decidual/cervical polyp, acetowhite epithelium, herpes genetalis, vaginal varices)
cohort: This study included 364 pregnant women with unexplained vaginal bleeding during their second or third trimester who underwent colposcopy at a tertiary care hospital between 2012 and 2022.
finding: Colposcopy was found to be a valuable diagnostic tool for pregnant women with unexplained vaginal bleeding in the second or third trimester, identifying the bleeding source in 22.8% of cases.
cross-section timing: Colposcopy examinations were performed during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at examination was 30.7 weeks.
